sources.entry: peft - A library for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large pretrained models.

summary.one_liner: PEFT is a Hugging Face library for parameter-efficient fine-tuning, adapting large pretrained models by training only a small set of extra parameters such as LoRA adapters.
summary.what_it_does: Provides implementations of parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods (LoRA is the main example shown) that freeze the base model and train a small number of added parameters. The get_peft_model function wraps a Transformers model with a PEFT config, and print_trainable_parameters reports the trainable fraction. Trained adapters are saved with save_pretrained and loaded onto a base model with PeftModel.from_pretrained. The README says PEFT integrates with Transformers (add_adapter, load_adapter, set_adapter), Diffusers for managing adapters, and Accelerate for distributed training and inference. It also mentions use with TRL for RLHF-style training and quantization such as QLoRA and 8-bit.
use_cases: fine-tune a large language model on a consumer GPU
train small LoRA adapters instead of full model checkpoints
switch between multiple task-specific adapters on one base model
reduce GPU memory needed for training large models
apply DPO or RLHF to an LLM with limited compute
how_to_run: Wrap a base model: model = get_peft_model(model, LoraConfig(...))
notable: Single get_peft_model call wraps any supported Transformers model with a LoRA or other PEFT config
Small adapter checkpoints (the README cites 19MB versus 11GB for the full T0_3B model)
Adapters can be loaded, switched, and managed through Transformers and Diffusers integrations
Works with quantization such as QLoRA and 8-bit training
caveats: The Transformers integration does not include every PEFT feature, such as merging adapters into the base model
Benchmarks in the README are on an A100 80GB GPU with more than 64GB CPU RAM, so results on other hardware will differ
Models not listed in the model support Space may need manual configuration
